source.title: Positive-Negative Momentum: Manipulating Stochastic Gradient Noise to Improve Generalization
source.authors: Zeke Xie; Li Yuan; Zhan-Xing Zhu; Masashi Sugiyama

record.file_problem: none; full paper text and appendices supplied
record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out performance of adaptive optimizer variants on word-level language modeling, a different optimizer comparison from the claim's Adam-versus-SGD evidence.
record.gate_note: The paper reports other optimizer comparisons in tables and figures, but the flattened Table 1 values do not support reliable model-to-value assignments. Its SGD-versus-PNM results change the optimizer's momentum/noise method and do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study's conventional optimizer baselines compare adaptive methods with momentum SGD on held-out image-classification error, bearing on V4. The extracted Penn TreeBank comparisons alone do not test V4 because they contain no SGD baseline.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that PNM variants generally improve on corresponding conventional momentum optimizers, including AdaPNM outperforming Adam and AMSGrad on Penn TreeBank. Their theoretical result concerns a tighter generalization-gap bound under stated assumptions, rather than an unconditional guarantee of better test performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces positive-negative momentum and compares its AdaPNM variant with Adam and AMSGrad; it does not reproduce the claim's adaptive-versus-SGD comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and optimizer choice; the reported language-model comparison is on word-level Penn TreeBank.

fits_no_version.finding: AdaPNM achieves Penn TreeBank perplexity 64.25 versus Adam 66.67 and AMSGrad 67.40.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Replacing conventional momentum with positive-negative momentum improves these adaptive optimizers on this language-modeling task.

fits_no_version.finding: PNM reduces noisy-label memorization and improves test performance relative to SGD on partially corrupted CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Amplifying stochastic gradient noise can improve robustness to partial label corruption.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 139, 2021
record.problems: The language-model comparison reports optimal test perplexities without uncertainty values. It compares AdaPNM with Adam and AMSGrad, not conventional adaptive optimizers with SGD. Other optimizer-comparison table values are flattened and do not support reliable model-to-value assignment.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 reports optimizer test errors, but its flattened layout does not reliably assign every value to model and dataset. Figures 1, 2, 5–11 contain additional optimizer results shown as plots; precise values are not stated in the text. These are not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and fully random-label training, near-perfect random-label fitting, and chance-level held-out performance. Partially corrupted labels do not establish this conjunction.
Width-dependent test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

Adaptive-versus-SGD performance on language modeling; broader hyperparameter tuning; switching from Adam to SGD. CIFAR adaptive methods use default learning rates rather than receiving the same learning-rate search as SGD.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover large-batch performance.
Dropout ablations, training-set-size dependence, and jointly removing dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with measured generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

missing.what: Conventional optimizer comparison: ResNet50/ImageNet momentum SGD top-1/top-5 errors 23.28%/6.75% versus AdamW 23.62%/7.09%.
Weight-decay-dependent conventional optimizer comparisons, including AdamW outperforming SGD and Adam on ResNet18 and VGG16/CIFAR-10 at weight decay 0.0001.
missing.locator: Table 3; Appendix B.1 and Appendix C

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V4 limits_scope verdict based on R1–R3. Replacement verdicts rely on conventional optimizer comparisons in the supplied text. Table 1 is declared in rows_left_out, so it is not duplicated in missing; Tables 2 and 3 are not declared there.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as network width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture generalization.
Comparison of conventional adaptive optimizers with SGD under the claim's limited tuning setup; broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching from Adam to SGD.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a measure of the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: LSTM
rows.size_stated: 14 million model parameters; 2 layers, 512 embedding dimensions, and 512 hidden dimensions
rows.operation_detail: Compared AdaPNM, Adam, and AMSGrad on word-level Penn TreeBank language modeling.
rows.note: Authors report these optimal test perplexities; this compares AdaPNM with adaptive baselines, not adaptive optimizers with SGD.
rows.check: The perplexities are correctly transcribed, but AdaPNM versus Adam and AMSGrad measures the proposed method's performance without an SGD comparator. It cannot establish V4.

rows.subject: LSTM
rows.size_stated: 14 million model parameters; 2 layers, 512 embedding dimensions, and 512 hidden dimensions
rows.operation_detail: Compared Adam on word-level Penn TreeBank language modeling.
rows.note: Lower test perplexity is better; Adam is worse than AdaPNM in this comparison.
rows.check: Adam's perplexity is correct, but its comparison with AdaPNM does not measure adaptive-versus-SGD generalization.

rows.subject: LSTM
rows.size_stated: 14 million model parameters; 2 layers, 512 embedding dimensions, and 512 hidden dimensions
rows.operation_detail: Compared AMSGrad on word-level Penn TreeBank language modeling.
rows.note: Lower test perplexity is better; AMSGrad is worse than AdaPNM in this comparison.
rows.check: AMSGrad's perplexity is correct, but its comparison with AdaPNM does not measure V4. The condition 'without amsgrad' is also incorrect for the AMSGrad comparator; it applies to AdaPNM and conventional Adam.

relationships.condition: CIFAR image classification with default adaptive learning rates and searched SGD learning rates
relationships.reason: From Table 1, already declared omitted: ResNet18/CIFAR-10 test errors are SGD 5.01%, Adam 6.53%, and AMSGrad 6.16%; VGG16 errors are 6.42%, 7.31%, and 7.14%. This supports the pattern under this asymmetric, limited tuning setup.
relationships.display_finding: The reported higher Adam and AMSGrad test errors than SGD under asymmetric learning-rate tuning remain unverified.

relationships.condition: ResNet50/ImageNet, learning-rate search for all optimizers, 150 epochs
relationships.reason: From Table 2, absent from the rows: AdamW has higher top-1/top-5 test errors, 23.62%/7.09%, than momentum SGD, 23.28%/6.75%. Decoupled weight decay does not eliminate the difference in this setting.
relationships.display_finding: The reported higher AdamW errors than momentum SGD despite decoupled weight decay remain unverified.

relationships.reason: From Table 1, already declared omitted: Padam reaches 6.15% test error versus SGD's 6.42%, showing that the adaptive-method disadvantage depends on optimizer choice.
relationships.display_finding: Padam reportedly achieved lower test error than SGD, but this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 with weight decay 0.0001 and decoupled weight decay in AdamW
relationships.reason: From Table 3, absent from the rows: AdamW improves on Adam and beats SGD on ResNet18 (5.33% versus 6.08% and 5.58%) and VGG16 (6.45% versus 7.04% and 6.92%), supporting V4's recovery qualification.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower AdamW error than both Adam and SGD remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: AdaPNM has lower optimal test perplexity than Adam and AMSGrad, but this comparison does not establish the claim's adaptive-versus-SGD pattern; see R1–R3.
